summary: The check carries the false premise: hermes-ignore-rules-required passes on HERMES_SKILL_PRELOAD; minimal fix is deleting the clause at line 186 and the constant/comment at 99-101.
The rule message repeats the claim (canonical and generated mirror); minimal fix drops the exception clauses and regenerates the .hermes mirror via sync-skills-hermes.cjs.

The exact test that must flip: test lines 118-119 asserting zero violations for -s cli-hermes and --skills=cli-hermes without --ignore-rules must become ['ignore-rules-required']; the comment at 116-117 is replaced by the A/B result.

The upstream source of the claim is Hermes live help as transcribed in the flag table ('...and preloaded skills injection'); cli-reference.md:88 already says every dispatch passes the flag, so the exemption is internally contradictory.

The persona dispatch contract is the second dependent: agent-delegation.md:48 and two playbook scenarios omit --ignore-rules whenever -s is in play, and HERMES-016's evidence note records the omission as compliance; fix adds the flag and drops the exception notes.

No second hard rule uses the premise: HERMES_SKILL_PRELOAD has a single use site, so the registry enforcement is singular; sk-git's unrelated hard_rules block was checked and has no preload carve-out.

Provenance: first-pass observation sourced from live help, 'closed' in the second pass by carving the exemption, now disproved by the commission-time A/B; dated reports stay as history, living surfaces are corrected.
The plugin's persona section already has a skill_view fallback for loading the persona skill when preload is unavailable, so passing --ignore-rules with -s loses nothing.
